notFound: Sony's own US, UK, Canada and Ireland sites (electronics.sony.com, sony.co.uk, sony.ca, store.sony.ca, sony.ie) refused every request from this environment (Akamai 'Access Denied' / 403, or no connection for store.sony.co.uk and store.sony.ie), so US, UK, CA and IE offers come from retailers' own pages (Abt, Hughes, Richer Sounds, The Brick, DID Electrical) and only Sony Mexico's own store (store.sony.com.mx) was read as a maker page.

Best Buy US and CA, B&H, Crutchfield, Walmart US and MX, Currys UK and IE, Argos UK, John Lewis, AO, Harvey Norman IE, Coppel and DID's didelectrical.ie domain were blocked, refused or did not answer (403, bot-block redirect, 502 or no response), so no offers from them were captured.

Costco (US, CA, UK, MX), Target, Walmart.ca, Euronics IE, Expert.ie, Power City, Sears MX, Cyberpuerta and Liverpool MX were reachable but not read for lack of fetch budget, so each market has offers from only the retailers named in the offers arrays.

No readable US, CA or MX page states an on-mode wattage for any Sony TV: Sony US/CA spec pages are blocked, Abt and The Brick spec tables have no watt line, ENERGY STAR's certified-television dataset (data.energystar.gov) holds no Sony records, and Sony Mexico's spec sheets leave the on-mode power lines blank ('-') and give only 0.5 W standby.

onModeWatts is therefore filled only where a UK Hughes-hosted product information sheet (EU energy label fiche) was read, and it is the on-mode power in SDR of the UK variant named in regionalModels (for example UK K-55S25M2 for US K55S20M2), not of the US or Mexican variant.

No energy-label sheet was read for BRAVIA 3 II (all sizes), BRAVIA 6 (all sizes), BRAVIA 7 II 50in and 85in, BRAVIA 8 55in and 77in, BRAVIA 8 II 55in, BRAVIA 9 II 115in, BRAVIA 3 43in, BRAVIA 9 75in, A95L, A90K, X90L, Z9K and W830K, because Hughes showed no fiche link for them or the model is not sold in the UK and no other primary page gave watts.

The 2025 BRAVIA 5 (UK XR55B) and BRAVIA 8 II (UK XR8M25B) fiches are an older 'Test report V.2.4' layout that prints no EPREL registration number, so eprel is null for those products although onModeWatts is set; the newer-layout fiches print an EPREL number, which is recorded.

Where a page labelled a regular price above its current price (Abt's 'Regular Price: Comp. Value', and Sony Mexico's list price against its selling price, which is assumed to be shown struck-through because the store renders prices client-side and could not be checked) the regular price was recorded and the lower current price was not, so real selling prices are lower (Sony Mexico K-55S20M2 lists MXN 19,499 but sells at MXN 9,999, and Abt sells K65XR70M2 at USD 1,798 against a regular USD 2,598).

Where a page displayed only a current price, that displayed price is recorded as a sale price because no regular price was shown: every Abt tile without a Comp. Value, Hughes' non-member price (its lower Rewards Plus member price and 'Save' flags are ignored), DID, The Brick (its product feed carries a compare-at price such as CAD 3,699.99 on the 65in BRAVIA 7 II that the page does not show, so the displayed CAD 2,199.95 is used) and Richer Sounds (whose page shows the current price plus a 'price history' line, for example GBP 1,599 now and GBP 1,899 until 18/08/26 on the 50in BRAVIA 7 II).

UK offers for BRAVIA 3 II (K-xxXR38M2PB, 43 to 100in) at Richer Sounds are flagged 'AS' (arriving soon) and out of stock, and the 115in BRAVIA 9 II is a pre-order, so those UK prices are listed prices that may not be orderable yet; Hughes also shows the 98in BRAVIA 7 II as 'Available Soon', DID shows K55S38B, K65S38B and K65XR55B as unavailable online, and The Brick's feed marks every Sony TV available although its 65in BRAVIA 7 II page shows zero inventory and a 'no longer available online' notice, so Brick availability is unconfirmed.

Sony Mexico's store shows zero stock for K-75XR50 (BRAVIA 5 75in) and K-65XR90M2 (BRAVIA 9 II 65in), and Abt marks K50S20M2, K83A60, XR48A90K and XR42A90K 'Call for availability', but all four still carry a listed price and are included.

BRAVIA 3 (2024, K-xxS30) is absent from Abt's current Sony list, so it has no US offer and its US model code was not confirmed on a US page: `model` is the code from The Brick (43, 50, 55, 85in) or from Hughes (65 and 75in, UK code K65S38B / K75S38B).

No model number or price was found on any page read for a BRAVIA 2 II 85in, BRAVIA 8 II 77in, BRAVIA 9 II 98in or any BRAVIA 6 in the UK or Ireland, so those sizes and markets are left out; DID lists no BRAVIA 3 II, 6, 7 II or 9 II, and The Brick lists no BRAVIA 3 65/75in, 7 II 98in or A95L 55in.

The 2025 BRAVIA 7 (K-xxXR70), the 2024 BRAVIA 9 at 65 and 85in, the X75WL, X85K, A95K and BRAVIA 8A sets and the 55in A95L and 98in X90L were seen only on Richer Sounds' listing flagged 'Finished' and out of stock (or as DID ex-display units), so they are not listed as current products.

Model years for the X90L (2023), Z9K (2022), W830K (2022) and BRAVIA 9 (2024) are Sony's launch years and are not stated on the pages read; BRAVIA 3's 2024 comes from The Brick's '2024 Model' titles, W800's 2021 from its EPREL market date, and the other years from Sony Mexico's 'Año del modelo' spec line or The Brick's model-year titles.

Panel class for the 'True RGB' BRAVIA 7 II and 9 II is recorded as Mini-LED because the pages call them 'LED RGB' (Sony Mexico) or 'RGB Mini LED' (Richer Sounds) and no allowed class fits an RGB-backlit LCD better; BRAVIA 8 (2024) is recorded as OLED as its retailers state and BRAVIA 8 II as QD-OLED.

refreshHz is the native panel rate from Sony Mexico's spec sheet or The Brick's tags (60 for BRAVIA 2 II, BRAVIA 3 and the HD sets, 120 for the rest), although the UK fiches print a 50 Hz default for BRAVIA 2 II and Richer Sounds lists 144 Hz for BRAVIA 5.

The US, UK, IE and Mexican codes of BRAVIA 2 II, 3, 3 II, 5, 7 II, 8 II and 9 II differ (for example US K65XR70M2, UK K65XR75M2B, Mexico K-65XR70M2) and are merged by series and size on the assumption they are the same television, which no primary page states outright, so a UK or IE wattage may not match the US or Mexican variant exactly.
